gates.detail: npm --prefix site run check: Test Files 1 failed | 4 passed (5); Tests 16 failed | 36 passed (52). All 16 failures are in src/play/browser/visual-baseline.browser.test.tsx ('visual baseline (W65.5)'), each failing with 'No existing reference screenshot found; a new one was created... Error: Matcher did not succeed in time.' Only *-chromium-linux.png and *-chromium-win32.png baselines are committed under site/src/play/browser/__screenshots__/ — no *-chromium-darwin.png baseline exists, so this host (macOS) cannot pass this suite locally. Not a code regression on this branch: CI runs this on ubuntu-latest inside the docs-template container, which has the linux baseline. The 16 newly-generated darwin screenshots were removed afterward via git clean -f; nothing was committed.

gates.reason: docs.ps1 is not present in this checkout. Per CLAUDE.md, docs.ps1 is generated by Invoke-SetupDocs (the docs-template installer) and is deliberately not committed; running it also requires Docker Desktop, which is up, so the missing script is the only blocker. The equivalent CI check on the pull request is 'Verify Documentation Build'.

gates.name: host tests
gates.reason: dotnet test src/host/SubZeroDev.GameEngine.Host.Tests/SubZeroDev.GameEngine.Host.Tests.csproj fails at NuGet restore: 'error NU1301: Failed to retrieve information about 'SubZeroDev.Platform.Hosting' from remote source https://nuget.pkg.github.com/The-Running-Dev/download/subzerodev.platform.hosting/index.json. Response status code does not indicate success: 401 (Unauthorized).' SubZeroDev.Platform.Hosting is published from the sibling SubZeroDev.Platform repository and requires a cross-repo GitHub Packages read token (REGISTRY_TOKEN in CI) not available in this local environment.

gates.name: host image smoke
gates.reason: host-image.yml's smoke job asserts REGISTRY_TOKEN is set before running dotnet test and building the Docker image. No such token is available locally, and host tests above already demonstrate the identical restore fails 401 Unauthorized without it, so a local docker build would fail at the same step. Docker itself is up and running locally, but the credential is not.
